node.title: Ampere's law and its applications to infinitely long straight wire. The solenoid, force on

questions.stem: A long solenoid has 25 turns per centimetre and carries a current of $0.80\,\text{A}$. What is the magnetic field well inside it? ($\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\text{T m A}^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: Inside a long solenoid $B = \mu_0 nI$, where $n$ must be in turns per metre. Here $n = 25\times100 = 2500\,\text{m}^{-1}$, so $B = (4\pi\times10^{-7})(2500)(0.80) = 2.5\times10^{-3}\,\text{T}$. Because $n$ counts turns per unit length, a mistake in the length unit changes the answer by a factor of one hundred.

optionRationale.1: Uses $n = 25$ per centimetre without converting to per metre.
optionRationale.3: This is $\mu_0 nI/2$, the value at an end of the solenoid, not at the middle.
optionRationale.4: Doubles the correct value, a stray factor of 2 from the straight-wire formula.

questions.objective: Compute the solenoid field from turns per unit length

questions.stem: An electron moves in a region of uniform magnetic field with its velocity parallel to the field. How does it move?
options: It continues in a straight line at constant speed, because the magnetic force is zero
It moves in a circle in a plane perpendicular to the field, because the magnetic force acts sideways
It speeds up along the field, because the magnetic force acts along the direction of motion
It moves in a parabola, because the magnetic force is constant and perpendicular to the field
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is $\vec F = q\,\vec v\times\vec B$, with magnitude $qvB\sin\theta$. For $\vec v$ parallel to $\vec B$ we have $\theta = 0$ and the force vanishes, so the electron keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed along the field.

optionRationale.2: A circle needs a velocity component perpendicular to $\vec B$; here there is none.
optionRationale.3: The magnetic force never acts along the velocity and can never change the speed.
optionRationale.4: A constant force would give a parabola, but here the magnetic force is zero.

questions.objective: Find the motion of a charge moving along a magnetic field

questions.stem: The magnetic field at a distance of $10\,\text{cm}$ from a long straight wire is $2.0\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}$. What current does the wire carry?
questions.explanation: Applying Ampere's law to a circle of radius $r$ about the wire gives $B = \mu_0 I/2\pi r$, so $I = 2\pi rB/\mu_0 = 2\pi(0.10)(2.0\times10^{-5})/(4\pi\times10^{-7}) = 10\,\text{A}$. The field falls as $1/r$, so doubling the distance would halve the field for the same current.

optionRationale.1: Leaves out the factor 2 in the denominator of the field formula, halving the current.
optionRationale.2: Puts a factor 2 in the wrong place, doubling the current.
optionRationale.3: Uses $B = \mu_0 I/r$ and drops the $2\pi$ entirely.

questions.objective: Find the current in a long wire from the field at a distance

questions.stem: A proton is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of $2000\,\text{V}$ and then enters a uniform magnetic field of $0.10\,\text{T}$ at right angles to the field. What is the radius of its circular path? ($m_p = 1.67\times10^{-27}\,\text{kg}$, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{C}$)
questions.explanation: The kinetic energy gained is $eV = \tfrac12 mv^2$, so $v = \sqrt{2eV/m} = 6.19\times10^{5}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. In the field the magnetic force supplies the centripetal force, $r = mv/eB = 6.5\,\text{cm}$. The sign of the charge only decides the sense in which the particle circulates; the speed gained and the radius depend on its magnitude.

optionRationale.1: Uses $eV = mv^{2}$ and so finds a speed smaller by a factor $\sqrt2$.
optionRationale.2: Uses $eV = \tfrac14 mv^{2}$ and so finds a speed larger by a factor $\sqrt2$.
optionRationale.4: This is the diameter of the circular path, not its radius.

questions.objective: Combine acceleration through a potential difference with circular motion in a field

questions.stem: An electron with speed $3.0\times10^{6}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ enters a uniform magnetic field of $2.0\times10^{-3}\,\text{T}$ with its velocity at $30^{\circ}$ to the field. What is the pitch of its helical path? ($m_e = 9.1\times10^{-31}\,\text{kg}$, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{C}$)
questions.explanation: The component along the field, $v\cos30^{\circ}$, is unchanged, while the perpendicular component makes the electron circle with period $T = 2\pi m/eB = 1.79\times10^{-8}\,\text{s}$. The pitch is the distance moved along the field in one period: $v\cos30^{\circ}\,T = 4.6\,\text{cm}$.

optionRationale.1: Uses $v\sin30^{\circ}$, the speed across the field, instead of the component along it.
optionRationale.3: Uses the full speed $v$ instead of its component along the field.
optionRationale.4: This is the radius of the circular projection, $mv\sin30^{\circ}/eB$, not the pitch.

questions.objective: Find the pitch of a helical path in a magnetic field

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about a charged particle in electric and magnetic fields.
A. The force on a charge moving in both fields is $q(\vec E + \vec v\times\vec B)$.
B. The magnetic force on a moving charge can change its kinetic energy.
C. A charge moving with speed $v = E/B$ through perpendicular crossed fields goes undeflected.
D. The electric force on a charge depends on the velocity of the charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: The Lorentz force $q(\vec E + \vec v\times\vec B)$ combines the two forces (A). In crossed fields the electric and magnetic forces cancel when $qE = qvB$, that is $v = E/B$ (C). The magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity and does no work, so B is false, and the electric force $q\vec E$ does not depend on velocity, so D is false.

optionRationale.1: Includes B, but the magnetic force does no work and cannot change the kinetic energy.
optionRationale.2: Contains two false statements, B and D, and leaves out the true A and C.
optionRationale.3: Includes D, but the electric force $q\vec E$ is the same for a charge at rest or in motion.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements about the Lorentz force and the velocity selector
